title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Jordan Lee
summary: Comprehensive operational guidance for Redwood Inference security controls: role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, centralized audit logging and retention, data residency and retention requirements, secure SDLC expectations, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and the process for requesting and documenting risk exceptions.
body:
Purpose:
This document consolidates security and compliance controls and operational procedures across RBAC & auth, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk and exceptions. It is intended for engineering, SRE, product security, and compliance owners who implement and verify controls for customer and internal workloads.

Scope:
Applies to: Redwood hosted services (control plane, API endpoints), Dedicated control plane components, Private deployment packaging, and associated operational tooling (CI/CD, observability, and ticketing systems). Excludes vendor-managed cloud service provider internal operations.

1) RBAC and Authentication
Overview:
- Purpose: enforce least-privilege access across control plane services, production clusters, observability, and secrets management.
- Primary systems: Identity Provider (IdP): Okta (SAML/OIDC), AWS IAM for cloud resources, Vault for secrets, and an internal SCIM-backed user->role sync for Redwood console.

RBAC model and roles:
- Global roles: admin, platform-engineer, infra-operator, product-owner, security-auditor, support-agent, read-only.
- Resource-scoped roles: project-admin, model-operator, deployment-manager, billing-reader.
- Principle: grant the minimum role necessary for job function; use project-scoped roles for customer isolation.

Authentication and MFA:
- All interactive user access requires IdP authentication with enforced MFA (hardware token or TOTP + push).
- Service-to-service authentication: short-lived mTLS certificates issued by our internal CA or IAM-assumed roles; no long-lived static credentials in code.

Onboarding/offboarding checklist (summary):
1. Create Okta account and join groups corresponding to team and project privileges.
2. Provision cloud roles (least privilege IAM policies).
3. Grant Vault access policies scoped to secrets required.
4. Document ownership in team wiki and create an access review ticket.

Access reviews and recertification:
- Quarterly automated access review for all groups and cloud roles. Security team sends remediation playbook when anomalies detected.
- Emergency revocation: security@redwood.com and oncall SRE can escalate to immediate session revocation and token invalidation.

2) Audit Logging
Design principles:
- Comprehensive, immutable logs for authentication events, RBAC changes, admin actions (deployments, rollout changes, secret access), and high-risk API calls (model downloads, export).
- Centralized collection in an append-only store (AWS S3 WORM with lifecycle + Athena index) and streaming to SIEM (Splunk/Chronicle).

Minimum log types and retention:
- Auth events (IdP): 7 years (for enterprise customers with compliance needs), default 1 year internal.
- Admin actions (console & API): 3 years.
- System audit (runtime access to model weights, KV cache exports): 7 years for private deployments where required.
- Observability/tracing: 90 days for high-cardinality traces; aggregated metrics 24 months.

Logging configuration (examples):
- Syslog/Fluentd configuration:
  * collect: /var/log/secure, /var/log/auth.log, application auth endpoints, kube-audit.
  * forward: kafka-cluster:9092 -> central-ingest -> s3-worm-bucket (encrypted SSE-KMS).

Integrity and access controls:
- Logs signed at ingest with HMAC and stored with object-level immutability.
- Only security and compliance roles have write/delete privileges on audit archives; read granted to authorized auditors via temporary access tokens.

3) Data Residency and Retention
Residency policy:
- Region selection is explicit at provisioning time. Hosted API defaults to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for EU-only customers. Dedicated and Private can be deployed to customer-specified regions or on-prem.
- Data-at-rest must be encrypted with KMS-managed keys (customer-managed keys for enterprise).

Retention baselines and overrides:
- Telemetry & metrics: default 24 months aggregated; 90 days raw.
- Logs & audit: default 1 year, adjustable per contract (up to 7 years) to satisfy regulatory requirements.
- Customer data (prompts, completions): default retention 30 days for hosted API; Dedicated/Private retention controlled by customer.

Data deletion and legal holds:
- Deletion request process: submit a ticket to privacy@redwood.com with customer ID and resources to delete. Automation will perform logical deletion, asynchronous purge from indices, and schedule object deletion respecting legal holds.
- Legal holds: Security & Legal can place a hold overriding retention; holds must be documented with justification and expiration.

4) Secure SDLC (Secure Software Development Lifecycle)
Policy summary:
- All production code follows the Secure SDLC checklist at merge time: static analysis, dependency scanning, secret scanning, architecture review for high-risk changes, and SCA.
- Threat modeling required for new features handling customer data or key control plane changes.

Gating controls and CI/CD pipeline:
- CI gates: unit tests, linters, SAST (Snyk/Checkmarx), dependency policy, secret-scan (git-secrets), container vulnerability scan.
- Pre-production: automated canary deploy to staging, integration tests, security smoke tests (auth, RBAC check), and canary monitoring for 24 hours before production rollout.

Release and change management:
- All releases tied to an ADR or PR that documents risks, rollback plan, owners, and SLO impact.
- Emergency patching process (SEV patch): security team coordinates with oncall infra to produce a CVE triage, hotfix branch, and an expedited rollout with post-incident review.

5) Incident Response - Security Procedures
Goals:
- Rapid containment, root cause analysis, customer notification when required, and preserving evidence for forensics and compliance.

On-call roles and escalation matrix:
- Triage lead (SRE), Incident commander (IC), Security investigator, Communications lead (legal + comms), Customer success liaison.

Initial triage playbook (numbered steps):
1. Detect: alert from monitoring, IDS, or external report.
2. Triage: determine scope and severity (SEV1–SEV4).
3. Contain: isolate affected services, rotate exposed keys, revoke compromised sessions.
4. Preserve evidence: snapshot logs, collect forensic images, enable high-fidelity logging if necessary.
5. Remediate: apply fixes, remove backdoors, restore from verified backups.
6. Notify: follow legal retention and breach notification timelines (per region and contract).
7. Postmortem: publish a blameless incident report with timeline, root cause, actions, and follow-ups within 7 business days for SEV1/SEV2.

Forensic checklist:
- Required artifacts: signed audit logs, timeline of relevant events, container images, cloud console session history, network flow captures.
- Storage: all artifacts ingested into secure evidence bucket (S3 with restricted role); cataloged in case management system.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Evidence collection principles:
- Automate evidence capture where possible: access review exports, policy attestations, scanning reports, test run history, infrastructure diffs.
- Maintain evidence indexes keyed by audit ID, customer ID (if applicable), and control IDs.

Standard evidence package (for a given control):
- Control description and owner.
- Configuration snapshot (YAML/JSON) and last change timestamp.
- Access review export CSV and remediation tickets.
- Audit log extract (signed) covering the relevant timeframe.
- SAST/DAST scan reports and remediation verification.

Evidence request process:
1. Compliance receives request (internal or auditor) with control IDs and timeframe.
2. Security triages and assembles package within SLA (standard: 5 business days; expedited: 48 hours with justification).
3. Deliver via secure transfer (SFTP with temporary credentials or secure link).

7) Risk and Exceptions Process
When an exception is required:
- Submit a Risk Exception Request (RER) in the governance tracker with: scope, justification, compensating controls, owner, and proposed duration (max 90 days without renewal).
- Criteria for approval: documented business need, no reasonable alternative, compensating controls demonstrated, and acceptance by Security + Legal for customer-facing impacts.

Approval workflow (numbered):
1. Requestor submits RER with owner and target mitigations.
2. Security reviews technical feasibility and required compensating controls.
3. Legal assesses regulatory/customer impact.
4. Risk Council (monthly) approves, rejects, or requires additional mitigations.
5. Approved exceptions are timeboxed and tracked; renewal requires fresh evidence.

Documented compensating controls examples:
- If full encryption-in-transit is temporarily infeasible for an integration, require VPN-only connectivity + per-connection audit logging and compensating SLA.
- If long-term log retention exceeds storage budget, implement targeted retention for critical controls and reduce retention elsewhere with documented rationale.

Owners and Escalation
- Documented owners: Security (primary), Eng-SRE (operationalization), Eng-Platform (tooling), Legal (contract/regulatory).
- Escalation: any unanswered RER or suspected control failure escalates to the Head of Security within 48 hours.

Appendices
A. Contact and oncall directory:
- Security Pager: +1-650-555-0123, security-oncall@redwood.com
- Incident channel: #incidents-security (Slack), follow runbook link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

B. Example CLI snippets
- Rotate a KMS key grant (AWS CLI):
  aws kms rotate-key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01

- Export access review (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN" https://console.redwood/api/v1/access-reviews?team=infra > infra-access-review.csv

C. Evidence table (text table)
| Control ID | Artifact | Retention | Owner |
| C-01 | Access review CSV | 3 years | Security |
| C-02 | Signed audit logs | 7 years | Eng-SRE |
| C-03 | CI/CD SAST report | 3 years | Eng-Developer-Experience |
